title: Protesters block the Lachin Corridor, cutting Nagorno-Karabakh off from Armenia
body:
On 12 December 2022 the Lachin Corridor, the only road linking Armenia and Nagorno-Karabakh, was blocked by people who described themselves as environmental activists. They cited alleged illegal mining and pollution at the Kashen and Drmbon mines. Two days earlier, on 10 December, a planned monitoring visit by Azerbaijani officials had been blocked by local residents and employees of the mining company. Azerbaijan's government denied that the protesters were responsible and said either Russian peacekeepers had closed the road or Nagorno-Karabakh's own government was preventing its citizens from using it.

By 28 December, according to Nagorno-Karabakh officials, shops had almost no fruit, vegetables, pulses, grains or sugar, with shortages of eggs, oil, flour, rice and tobacco. The International Committee of the Red Cross delivered ten tonnes of medicine and baby food on 25 December, the only confirmed aid delivery, which Stepanakert's government said would last about ten days. More than 1,000 Karabakh Armenians were unable to return home, and about a dozen patients were transported from Stepanakert to Yerevan for treatment.

On 28 December Nagorno-Karabakh's government suspended the Kashen copper-molybdenum mine pending an international examination and asked the United Nations to send an inspection team. Acting foreign minister Davit Babayan called for sanctions against Azerbaijan and warned that an entire nation would starve if the road stayed closed. On 3 January 2023 Armenia's Foreign Ministry proposed an international fact-finding mission.
